summary: San Marino's Foreign Ministry says visitors must cross the Schengen Area to reach San Marino, so those from outside it need the authorisations to enter the Schengen Area, applied for at the embassy or consulate of a Schengen state where they live. The UK says you do not pass through border controls to enter San Marino, and San Marino requires a permit of stay for stays over 30 days.

tips.text: You have to travel through Italy to reach San Marino. The UK FCDO says there are no border controls to pass on entry, but your passport must carry a valid entry stamp from a Schengen country.
The UK government says you can travel without a visa to the Schengen Area and San Marino for up to 90 days in any 180-day period, with visits to Schengen countries counting towards the 90 days.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for San Marino?
faq.answer: San Marino's Foreign Ministry says visitors must cross the Schengen Area to reach San Marino, so travellers from outside it need the authorisations to enter the Schengen Area, applied for at the embassy or consulate of a Schengen state where they live. The UK says you do not pass through border controls to enter San Marino but need a valid Schengen entry stamp in your passport.

faq.question: Does visiting San Marino use up a single-entry Schengen visa?
faq.answer: No official source we could read addresses single-entry Schengen visas and San Marino. The UK says you do not need to pass through border controls to enter San Marino, but your passport must contain a valid entry stamp from a Schengen area country.

faq.question: How long can I stay in San Marino?
faq.answer: The UK says visa-free travellers can stay in the Schengen Area and San Marino for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. San Marino's Foreign Ministry says that to stay more than 30 days you must go to the Gendarmeria's Foreigners Office (Ufficio Stranieri) within those 30 days and apply for a permit of stay.
